About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic's Infrastructure organization is foundational to our mission of developing AI systems that are reliable, interpretable, and steerable. The systems we build determine how quickly we can train new models, how reliably we can run safety experiments, and how effectively we can scale Claude to millions of users — demonstrating that safe, reliable infrastructure and frontier capabilities can go hand in hand.

Cluster Infra owns the full lifecycle of compute clusters at Anthropic. We build agent-driven automation for cluster provisioning and lifecycle management across all major cloud providers and our own datacenters. Our systems stand up clusters that are interconnected with high bandwidth, secure-by-default, and able to automatically drain and recover in response to failure. As a Staff engineer on this team, you'll set the technical direction for how Anthropic brings compute online - at a moment when the scale of that compute is growing faster than at almost any company in the world.

Key responsibilities

• Own the technical strategy and roadmap for agent-driven cluster lifecycle management - provisioning, updates and decommissioning
• Partner across teams to ensure new compute capacity is ingested on time
• Align with partner teams on physical build-out and leverage cloud solutions to deliver high-bandwidth inter-cluster connectivity
• Collaborate with security owners to ensure clusters are provisioned secure-by-default
• Define and drive strategy on cluster scalability, homogeneity and fault tolerance
• Work closely with cloud providers and internal research, inference and product teams to shape long-term compute, data, and infrastructure strategy
• Establish and evolve operational-excellence practices: incident response, postmortem culture and on-call health
• Support the growth of engineers around you through technical mentorship and coaching

Minimum qualifications

• Deep expertise in distributed systems, reliability, and cloud platforms (e.g., Kubernetes, IaC, AWS/GCP/Azure)
• Strong proficiency in at least one systems language (e.g., Rust, Go, or Python), IaC proficiency with Terraform.
• Track record of leading complex, multi-quarter technical initiatives spanning multiple teams or systems
• Ability to build alignment across senior stakeholders and communicate effectively at all levels

Preferred qualifications

• 10+ years of software engineering experience, including time as a technical lead setting direction for a team
• Experience operating large-scale compute infrastructure at hyperscale (100+ clusters, 10K+ nodes)
• Depth in one or more of: Kubernetes internals, cluster provisioning and management systems, cluster orchestration systems (Mesos, Borg-like)
• Experience with cloud networking: VPC design and peering, Shared VPC/Transit Gateway, Cloud Interconnect/Direct Connect, Cloud NAT, cross-cloud private connectivity, BGP and route control, edge load balancing and DDoS mitigation (Cloud Armor / AWS Shield)
• Experience with cluster and host networking: CNI (Cilium), eBPF, NetworkPolicy, multi-NIC, sFlow, service mesh (Istio/Envoy/Linkerd, mTLS)
• Experience with cluster security: pod security standards and admission control, RBAC and least-privilege IAM, node and container hardening, supply-chain/image provenance
• Deep experience with infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Atlantis), workflow orchestration (Temporal, Argo Workflows)
• Skill in quickly understanding systems design tradeoffs and keeping track of rapidly evolving software systems

Annual Salary:

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. About the Role

As a Technical Program Manager, Robotics Facilities, you will serve as the Robotics point-of-contact for cross-functional partners supporting the design and construction of Robotics sites. You will consolidate requirements, priorities, and decisions across Robotics disciplines and route those inputs through your counterpart, who manages design and construction partners and coordinates their workstreams.

You will clarify requirements, coordinate technical and operational inputs, manage dependencies and changes, and drive timely decisions through planning, design, construction, commissioning, and handover. This role calls for sound program judgment as research and operational needs evolve.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 4 days a week.

In this role, you will:

- Consolidate requirements, priorities, and decisions across Robotics research, engineering, and operations teams, providing the Real-Estate Workplace counterpart with a clear and coordinated view of Robotics needs.

- Translate Robotics workflows and equipment needs into documented requirements for floor layouts, utilities, network connectivity, environmental conditions, material flow, physical access, and operational support, working with technical owners to define acceptance criteria.

- Coordinate Robotics design reviews, ensuring technical owners assess proposals, resolve open questions, and confirm that agreed requirements are reflected in project documents.

- Track Robotics deliverables and dependencies against project milestones, surface risks and changes early, and secure decisions needed to keep work moving.

- Coordinate with Legal, Finance, Security, IT, Environmental Health & Safety, and other specialists to resolve issues affecting Robotics requirements and readiness.

- Coordinate Robotics readiness for equipment installation, moves, commissioning, and operational handover, with clear ownership and follow-through.

- Identify facility constraints that slow experimentation or operations, and use feedback from Robotics teams to improve requirements and handover practices for future projects.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have experience leading technical programs involving hardware and physical infrastructure, ideally in robotics, laboratories, advanced manufacturing, or similarly complex environments.

- Can reconcile competing priorities across technical and operational teams and translate evolving needs into clear requirements and acceptance criteria.

Product를 지속적으로 발전 시켜서 고객에게 최상의 경험을 선사하기 위해서 끊임없이 노력하고 있습니다

We are hiring a Deal and Contract Operations Manager to join our Business Operations team in San Francisco. In this role, you will design and own the end-to-end deal and contracting processes mainly by supporting and training deal owners on contracting workflows, including operational ownership of our contracting tool, acting as the escalation point before deals get stuck, coordinating across internal approver teams such as Legal, Tax, and Finance to keep deals moving forward, and ensuring every signed partner has a smooth onboarding experience by involving the right stakeholders pre- and post-close.

Because you sit at the center of every deal, you will have a unique vantage point to spot what needs to be standardized, automated, or tooled across the deal lifecycle, and coordinate with the rest of the functions under Bizops (i.e. Sales Ops, Order Management, Business Systems etc.) to make it happen. You will use that perspective to build frameworks, drive process automation, and continuously reduce the time it takes to get from contract signing to customer onboarding, ensuring downstream teams like Partner Success, Order Management, and Logistics are engaged at the right time.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and maintain the end-to-end contract operations processes, from template selection support through approval alongside Legal so that deal owners (i.e. Business Development and Partner Success teams) can move deals through the process efficiently and with minimal friction.
- Project-manage deals from contract signing through customer onboarding, ensuring downstream teams (Partner Success, Order Management, RevOps, Logistics) are engaged at the right time prior to deal close, and that non-standard terms are highlighted and passed along to the correct stakeholders.
- Troubleshoot Contract Lifecycle Management (i.e.) workflow issues, advise on routing and approvals, and unblock bottlenecks so deal owners can keep momentum.
- Train and equip Business Development teams to be self-sufficient in the contracting process: how to create CLM workflows, select the right contract template and deal term configuration, route to the correct approvers, and anticipate approval requirements
- Ensure contract templates are properly created and maintained within the CLM system in adherence with the Amazon policy, and assist Business Development with escalating redlines to Legal and driving alignment on accepted terms.
- Use your centralized vantage point across all deals to spot patterns and identify what needs to be standardized, automated, or tooled, translating those insights into process improvements that make the entire deal lifecycle faster and more consistent.
- Lead process automation initiatives with the goal of decreasing contract throughput time and increasing deal signing velocity.
- Develop lightweight tooling and streamlined processes for higher-frequency, lower-complexity deals (e.g., direct Enterprise deals), including enabling 3P sales reps to independently handle NDAs and select contracting workflows on our behalf.
- Develop AI-based mechanisms to handle specialized deals with exception approvals for non-standard requests.
- Collaborate closely with Sales Ops and Order Management to feed process automation ideas and ensure the right tooling gets built to reduce manual effort across the deal-to-onboarding lifecycle.
- Continuously improve the onboarding experience for B2B customers by removing avoidable friction points, with decreasing time-to-onboard as a key success metric.

A day in the life
You might start your morning checking in on active deals in Contract Central, spotting one that's waiting on Tax approval and flagging to the BD owner how long that step usually takes. By midday, you could be helping a Business Development lead pick the right contract template and approval routing for a non-standard deal, or bringing Partner Success and Order Management in ahead of a signing so onboarding starts smoothly. Afternoons often involve working with Legal, Finance, and Sales Ops to clear a recurring bottleneck, followed by turning what you've seen across deals into a standard workflow or an automation idea. You will regularly train deal owners on contracting best practices and present recommendations to leaders on reducing time from signing to onboarding.

About the team
Our team keeps eero's partner deals and orders moving, from contract signing through delivery. As part of eero Business Operations, we work closely with Business Development, Partner Success, Legal, Finance, Order Management, and Logistics teams to build the processes and tools that help ISPs, Enterprise customers, and retail partners around the world get eero into their customers' homes and businesses. We value ownership, creative problem-solving, and using AI and automation to take manual work off our plates so we can focus on our partners. As we grow into new channels and regions, you will have the opportunity to shape how we scale deal and contract operations.

About the Team

The Storage organization builds and operates the online stateful systems and abstractions that DoorDash Engineering depends on: reliable, efficient, secure, and easy to use. Within Storage, the Distributed Key Value team owns the storage platform that powers business-critical workloads across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo.

These systems sit on the Tier-0 critical path. They serve millions of QPS across multiple regions and underpin how hundreds of engineering teams build reliable systems at massive scale.

About the role

DoorDash's storage abstraction platform is a unified data-access layer that sits in front of our databases and decouples application teams from the underlying storage engines, similar to modern data-gateway and key-value / time-series data-abstraction platforms. Nearly every request that touches persistent data flows through it.

As DoorDash scales 10x–100x across new verticals, global expansion, and acquisitions, this platform is where the hardest distributed-storage problems live — latency at the tail, request routing, and reliability under exponential load. We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to be the domain specialist for the storage abstraction platform: a deep, opinionated technical leader who owns the reliability, performance, and correctness of the platform at scale, sets its technical direction, and raises the execution bar across the storage organization.

You must be located in the New York Metro Area, Bay Area or Seattle for this hybrid position. You will report to the Engineering Manager on our Distributed Key Value team within the Storage organization.

You're excited about this opportunity because you will…

• Own the reliability, performance, and correctness of the storage abstraction platform at scale, independently leading resolution of mission-critical issues in ambiguous, high-pressure situations.
• Set technical direction for the platform — the storage abstraction and data-access layer, provider model, caching, and routing — owning the architecture, quality, and long-term approach as it scales.
• Work deep in the data plane — proxy, KV, CDC, and routing — on the problems that define a Tier 0 system: p99/p999 latency, request routing, hot partitions, GC/MVCC behavior, and failure isolation.
• Shape the client surface — thin/thick providers, polyglot code generation, and SDKs — that connects application services to the platform.
• Act as a force multiplier and trusted technical advisor: raise the execution and quality bar for your team and partners, mentor senior engineers, and influence roadmaps beyond your immediate scope.
• Take end-to-end ownership of the platform lifecycle — guiding customers from onboarding through adoption, driving the offering forward and expanding its impact.
• Design and operate systems built for 100x growth, proactively engineering for exponential load rather than reacting to it, and eliminating single points of failure through documentation, automation, and shared ownership.
• Translate ambiguous business needs into durable, storage-owned solutions, and be an opinionated domain expert on how storage problems are best solved.

We're excited about you because…

• 10+ years building large-scale distributed systems, with deep expertise in at least one Tier 0 storage / data-plane system (distributed KV, database internals, caching, or a storage proxy/control plane).
• Experience with storage abstraction layers or data-access gateways that decouple applications from the underlying databases — e.g., data-gateway or key-value / time-series data-abstraction platforms, or comparable in-house systems. Deep experience building or operating a large-scale distributed data store — such as DynamoDB, RocksDB, or ZippyDB — is an equally strong fit.
• Expertise in low-latency, high-throughput systems — tail-latency optimization, hot-partition and load balancing/routing, backpressure, and failure isolation.
• Strong Go experience in production distributed systems.
• Deep, hands-on grasp of storage internals: MVCC, GC/compaction, consistency models, replication, and/or CDC.
• Proven ownership of Tier 0 / mission-critical services — on-call leadership, incident resolution under ambiguity, and capacity and performance work at scale.
• Demonstrated Staff-level technical leadership: setting direction across teams, acting as a force multiplier, and driving org-wide architectural decisions.
• Kubernetes and cloud-native infrastructure; strong observability instincts (metrics, tracing, profiling).
• You have proficiency in using AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) in the full software development lifecycle, including designing, generating code, testing, monitoring and releasing software

Preferred

• Cassandra (or comparable wide-column/NoSQL) internals and operations.
• Built client/SDK, code-generation, or provider/abstraction layers across polyglot clients.
• Open-source contributions to storage, database, or distributed-systems projects.

Compensation

The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future.

In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information.

DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others.

To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here.

See below for paid time off details:

• For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year.
• For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week).

At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods.

DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. About the role

If you’ve been in the BAS world a while, you know the difference between a job that just keeps you busy and one that keeps you engaged, respected, and growing.

At Automated Logic, a Carrier Company, our Managers describe this as the place where they finally found both challenge and balance. A place that trusts your judgment, values your craftsmanship, and gives you the tools and autonomy to make an impact.

As a Mission Critical Field Service Supervisor, you’ll be the expert voice on-site — a professional with deep knowledge and highly developed technical expertise in Field Service work. You’ll be counted on to deliver the kind of precision work our customers remember.

Our long-tenured people put it simply:

“I finally found it. Not just a job. Not just a paycheck. A work home.”

If that sounds like what you’ve been looking for, we’d like to welcome you home too.

At Automated Logic, we believe in investing in our people. As a Supervisor, you’ll have access to:

● Professional Development: Training programs, certifications, and continuing education in BAS technologies and leadership.

● Career Pathways and Leadership Opportunities: Opportunities to advance into other roles as well as mentor junior staff and contribute to strategic initiatives that shape our service delivery.

● Recognition & Rewards: Recognition programs that celebrate your contributions.

What you’ll gain

● Health & wellness benefits (from day one), 401k, paid time off and competitive wages - along with fleet vehicle eligibility (with personal use allowance).

● Stability and respect. Many of our Managers have been here 10–20 years — because their work, time, and expertise are valued.

● Freedom to execute. You’ll own your projects, make field calls, and collaborate closely with engineers and PMs who trust your expertise.

● Continuous learning. Access to advanced training in WebCTRL®, networking, integration, and system analytics.

● Balance and culture. Leadership that respects family time, and a team that looks out for one another.

About this role

As Automated Logic continues to expand across Virginia's rapidly growing data center market, this role will play a critical part in supporting some of the most complex and demanding mission critical facilities in the world. From hyperscale cloud campuses to high-availability computing environments, you'll lead teams delivering building automation systems where uptime, reliability, and precision execution are essential. This is an opportunity to work at the forefront of data center technology while developing the next generation of field engineering talent.

Mission Critical Experience. Direct involvement supporting large-scale data center and mission critical facilities where building automation systems are integral to operational reliability, energy optimization, and continuous uptime.

Join a team supporting some of the largest and fastest-growing data center and mission critical facilities in North America.

As a Mission Critical Field Service Supervisor, you will lead and develop a team of Field Engineers responsible for delivering high-quality building automation solutions within data centers and other critical environments where uptime, reliability, and operational continuity are essential. You will partner with Project Managers, customers, and trade partners to safely execute projects, coordinate resources, maintain schedules, and ensure technical excellence across all phases of project delivery.

Key Responsibilities

• Lead, mentor, and develop a team of Field Engineers.
• Coordinate field execution for mission critical and data center projects.
• Support project planning, scheduling, staffing, commissioning, and technical checkout activities.
• Ensure compliance with customer change management, safety, and operational readiness requirements.
• Partner with Project Managers to manage resources, budgets, quality, and customer expectations.
• Provide technical leadership and troubleshooting support for BAS installations, integrations, and commissioning activities.

• 3+ years of experience in the HVAC, Construction or building automation and controls industry
• 1+ years of experience with the Microsoft Office Suite, proficient in Microsoft Excel.
• Clean and valid driver’s license

• Experience interacting with a large and diverse number of simultaneous challenges, requiring knowledge of multiple disciplines.

• Experience supporting data centers, healthcare, pharmaceutical, manufacturing, or other high-availability facilities.
• Knowledge of chilled water systems, critical cooling applications, and facility operations.
• Experience working under formal change management and outage planning processes.
• Strong leadership, communication, and team development skills.
